scenes.title: Room for Our Rivals
scenes.summary: On Friday morning, F1 and F2 ask M2 to welcome the stranded Clock-Square musicians and woodcarver into {SHOW}'s east arcade for Saturday morning.
scenes.intro: Early Friday morning at the front desk of {SHOW}, {F1} and {F2} lay a clean courtyard sketch in front of {M2} before he finishes his first sip of coffee. Listen first.
story: M2
Let me understand this clearly: Clock-Square withdraws, leaving {SHOW} clear favourite for first prize?
F1
About that, {M2}... {F2} and I drew two extra guest tables along our east arcade.
F2
Their two young flute players rehearsed for months, and their woodcarver carved fifty spoons!
M2
Wait—you want to invite the three-time Golden Plaque champions INSIDE our courtyard?!
F1
Only their stranded morning musicians and craft table so their hard work is not wasted!
M2
Suppose the secret judges give the Golden Plaque to THEIR flutes inside MY courtyard?!
F2
And suppose we win a shiny trophy while two neighbours sit home staring at a trench?
M2
Hmm... put like that, a solitary trophy sounds remarkably chilly at breakfast.
F1
Besides, {F3} says two flutes plus walnut piano will sound glorious together!
M2
Still, twenty extra visitors means double tea and very crowded flagstones, ladies...
F2
Before you decide, boss, step into Room Nine—{M1} left something on the table for you.
M2
When {M1} leaves silent visual aids on tables, I know I am outnumbered!
scenes.outro: Torn between a guaranteed trophy and neighbourly kindness, {M2} steps into Room 9 to see what {M1} left waiting. See you next time.

scenes.title: Remember the Brass Motto
scenes.summary: Inside Room 9, M1 points to the freshly polished oval brass plaque on the table, convincing M2 to telephone the Clock-Square team with a warm Saturday invitation.
scenes.intro: Morning light gleams off the polished oval brass plaque resting on green velvet inside Room 9, where {M1} and {F3} stand calmly beside the walnut piano as {M2} walks in. Let us listen in first.
story: M2
All right, {M1}, why is our founding gate plaque sitting beside the piano bench?
M1
Before I bolt it onto the stone arch at noon, read the bottom line again.
M2
Warm bread, quiet shade, and an open gate make strangers into friends.
F3
Notice the founder did not write: Keep the gate half closed to win a prize, {M2}.
M1
For a hundred years, this house shared shade whenever {STREET} needed a dry roof.
M2
You two arranged this whole speech before breakfast, did you not?
F3
Not a speech, {M2}—just an invitation for you to be the host your aunt raised.
M2
Pull down my glasses—no, they are already down—hand me the lobby telephone!
M1
Here is the Clock-Square coordinator number written in pencil on a clean card.
M2
I shall offer them the sunny east arcade, two linen tables, AND free morning mint tea!
F3
Bravo, {M2}! Tell their two flute players to bring sheet music in G major!
M1
And once you hang up, bring my screwdriver—time to put this brass home.
scenes.outro: A hundred-year-old brass motto wins the day in thirty seconds, and {SHOW} opens its arms to its neighbours! See you at the gate next time.

scenes.title: Four Bronze Screws Home
scenes.summary: At noon on Friday outside the front arch, M1 screws the gleaming oval founding plaque back into its four original limestone holes while F1 and M2 cheer.
scenes.intro: Twelve chimes ring from the distant clock tower on Friday noon as {M1} holds his brass-handled screwdriver against the oval plaque beside the front gate while {F1} and {M2} watch proudly from {STREET}. Listen first.
story: M1
Top left screw snug, bottom right screw snug, top right, and bottom left... home.
F1
Step back onto the cobbles, {M2}—our founding oval plaque is back after twenty years!
M2
Look how the noon sunlight catches the polished brass right below the cream-and-gold pennants!
F1
Rule One, Rule Two, AND Rule Three of the Historic Courtyard Festival—officially complete!
M2
And guess what the Clock-Square coordinator said on the telephone ten minutes ago!
F1
Did their woodcarver and their two young flute players accept our east arcade spot?!
M2
Nearly cried with relief—and offered to lend us twelve extra porcelain teacups for tomorrow!
M1
See that, boss? Good neighbours always bring extra teacups.
F1
Look at people walking down {STREET} already stopping to read our gleaming brass motto!
M2
Tomorrow at ten sharp, this gate opens to the whole city!
M1
Save the victory bows for tomorrow evening; we still have tables and lights to check.
F1
And {F3} and {M3} are inside Room Nine right now planning the shared flute concert!
scenes.outro: Four bronze screws anchor twenty years of wandering brass back onto {STREET}—with twelve borrowed teacups on the way! See you next time.

scenes.title: Sharing the Programme
scenes.summary: Inside Room 9, F3 and M3 arrange a seamless Saturday morning musical programme weaving piano, neighbourly violin, and the visiting Clock-Square flutes together.
scenes.intro: Friday afternoon inside peaceful Room 9, {F3} pencils notes onto clean manuscript paper at the walnut piano while {M3} tests chair angles near the open green shutters. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: M3
If the two flute players stand right beside screen number one, listen to this angle, {F3}.
F3
Woodwind notes rise gently toward the shade tree while the piano supports them underneath!
M3
How should we divide the Saturday morning music between ten and twelve noon?
F3
At ten sharp, you and I open with our cheerful four-hand welcome duet.
M3
Then at half past ten, the two Clock-Square flutes play three folk dances!
F3
And at eleven, number ten brings his violin so all five of us play!
M3
Wait—piano, violin, AND two flutes playing the Courtyard Waltz together at eleven?!
F3
I just wrote a simple two-flute harmony part on this sheet in twenty minutes!
M3
{F3}, is there any musical puzzle on earth you cannot solve before tea?
F3
Give a retired teacher a sharp pencil and happy students, {M3}, and time flies.
M3
Let us run the new harmony bars once so I know every bass cue cold.
F3
Hands ready on C major—tomorrow morning, {STREET} hears a five-piece ensemble!
scenes.outro: A solo waltz grows into a joyful five-piece neighbourhood ensemble inside sunlit Room 9! See you at dawn next time.

scenes.title: Sixty Twists at Dawn
scenes.summary: At six-thirty on Festival Saturday morning, F2, M4, and F1 braid and glaze sixty golden honey-fig almond twists in the warm café kitchen.
scenes.intro: Festival Saturday dawns clear and golden over {CITY}! At half past six inside the bustling café kitchen, {F2}, {M4}, and {F1} work side by side rolling fragrant cinnamon-almond dough into braided rings. Listen first.
story: F2
Tray three into the top oven, tray four into the bottom oven—forty twists baking!
M4
And twenty golden twists already cooling on the wire rack, smelling like heaven!
F1
My hands can officially braid honey-fig dough with both eyes closed now, {F2}!
F2
Keep both eyes open while brushing the warm orange-blossom honey glaze, apprentice!
M4
How many pots of fresh mint and black tea should we steep by quarter to ten?
F2
Six big ceramic pots, plus hot water ready in both copper urns behind the counter.
F1
Look out the kitchen window: {M3} is already carrying out the extra wooden craft tables!
M4
Once tray four comes out at seven-fifteen, I go help my brother set the east arcade!
F2
Take three warm twists on a plate for you and {M3}—builders eat first today!
F1
Zero burnt edges, sixty shining twists, and two hours left before ten sharp!
M4
Save one corner twist for {M1} too—he has been sweeping cobbles since six!
F2
Aprons straight, team—today {SHOW} feeds half of {CITY}!
scenes.outro: Sixty braided honey-fig twists gleam on cooling racks before eight in the morning as courtyard setup hits full stride! See you outside next time.

scenes.title: Setting the East Arcade
scenes.summary: At eight-thirty in the sunny courtyard, M3 and M4 welcome the Clock-Square tables along the east arcade while F2 stacks the rock-solid three-tier brass stand.
scenes.intro: Morning sun climbs over the courtyard tree at half past eight. {M3} and {M4} align crisp linen tables beside the four cedar acoustic screens while {F2} loads golden pastries onto the gleaming three-tier brass stand. Let us listen in first.
story: M4
Look at that east arcade, {M3}: rosemary pots, cedar screens, and sunlit craft tables!
M3
The Clock-Square woodcarver just dropped off his carved spoons—he loved the light here!
F2
And watch me place twist number thirty right on top of our three-tier brass tower!
M4
Not a wobble, not a lean, not a single flying brass acorn anywhere!
F2
Give credit to {M1} and his toothed steel lock washer underneath the base!
M3
Look up at the balcony-to-tree cords too: twenty-four paper lanterns ready for dusk.
M4
Plus twenty-eight numbered birch clothespins clipping every white napkin tight against morning breezes!
F2
Everything we fixed or invented over the past month is working together in one courtyard!
M3
From Room Nine and its walnut piano to the gold-leaf map inside the lobby!
M4
Speaking of the lobby, has anyone checked whether {M2} put on white gloves again?!
F2
{F1} and {F3} are inspecting the boss right now—go check the gate, brothers!
M3
Fifteen minutes to ten, and voices are already gathering outside on {STREET}!
scenes.outro: Every repair from four seasons stands proud in the morning sun as festival footsteps gather outside on {STREET}! See you inside Room 9 next time.

scenes.title: Glasses on the Nose
scenes.summary: At nine-forty-five inside Room 9, F1 and F3 straighten M2's jacket, verify he has only one pair of glasses squarely on his nose, and calm his pre-opening nerves.
scenes.intro: Quarter to ten inside glowing Room 9! {F3} adjusts a small sprig of rosemary on {M2}'s jacket lapel while {F1} conducts a strict final pre-opening check. Listen first.
story: F1
Final inspection at nine forty-five: blue jacket brushed, shoes polished, zero white gloves!
M2
My knees are shaking slightly, ladies—listen to how many people are chatting on {STREET}!
F3
Happy weekend neighbours excited to see what {SHOW} built behind its limestone arch, {M2}.
F1
Most important check of the morning: how many pairs of glasses do you have on?
M2
One pair, resting squarely on the bridge of my nose, secured with pure willpower!
F3
And zero secret-judge detective games today, promise us both, {M2}?
M2
I promise solemnly: water-meter readers and festival judges receive the exact same smile!
F1
The two young flute players from Clock-Square are tuned and smiling beside your piano, {F3}!
F3
And our friend from number ten just rosined his violin bow by the doorway!
M2
Look at {M1} waving to us from the closed iron street gate—five minutes to ten!
F1
Time for the owner of {SHOW} to go open his front gate on the chime!
M2
Walk beside me, {F1}—let us welcome {CITY} in together!
scenes.outro: One pair of glasses on one proud nose—now only the heavy iron gate latch stands between {SHOW} and ten sharp! Final scene of Episode 5!

scenes.title: Five Minutes to Ten
scenes.summary: At one minute to ten inside the archway, M2 tugs the heavy iron gate handle in excitement and finds it stuck fast from cool morning dew—just as the first clock chime strikes!
scenes.intro: At nine fifty-nine inside the stone entrance arch, fifty cheerful festival visitors wait just beyond the iron gate on {STREET}. {M2} steps forward proudly between {F1} and {M1} to practise opening on the stroke of ten. Listen first.
story: F1
Sixty seconds to ten! Look through the iron bars at all those smiling faces!
M2
Photographers, families with guidebooks, neighbours—stand back while I unlatch the main gate!
M1
Easy on that old iron bar, boss; cool morning dew settled on the hinge pin.
M2
Nonsense, I open this gate every day... pull... tug... WHY IS IT NOT MOVING?!
F1
{M2}! Stop pulling straight backward with both hands—you jammed the heavy iron tongue!
M2
IT IS STUCK! Listen—there goes chime number one from the municipal clock tower!
M1
Step aside half a foot, boss, and let my brass oil spout reach the latch slot.
F1
Chime three, chime four... fifty people outside are watching you through the bars, {M2}!
M2
Smile and wave casually through the ironwork as if this is dramatic suspense!
M1
Two drops of oil in—now tell the boss our number-one house rule, {F1}.
F1
Chime eight, chime nine—LIFT THE HANDLE SLIGHTLY FIRST BEFORE YOU PULL!
M2
Chime ten—lifting slightly first, and... CLICK! Swing both gates wide open!
scenes.outro: Saved on the tenth chime by two drops of oil and our oldest house rule, the gates of {SHOW} swing wide open! End of Episode 5—see you in the Season 4 finale!
